We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in 5d^2 double perovskites.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Polarons can switch the octupolar order, revealing a mechanism for controlling multipolar phases.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into polaron-magnetism interplay in complex oxides, but are not relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Ultrafast Formation Of A Photoinduced Hidden State Driven By A Bond-Order Wave In A Metal-Organic Framework
authors: Samiran Banu, Tatsuya Amano, Takahisa Kato, Kou Takubo, Yoichi Okimoto, Shinya Koshihara, Yohei Kawakami, Hirotake Itoh, Wataru Kosaka, Hitoshi Miyasaka, Shinichiro Iwai, Akira Takahashi, And Tadahiko Ishikawa
abstract:
Author(s): Samiran Banu, Tatsuya Amano, Takahisa Kato, Kou Takubo, Yoichi Okimoto, Shinya Koshihara, Yohei Kawakami, Hirotake Itoh, Wataru Kosaka, Hitoshi Miyasaka, Shinichiro Iwai, Akira Takahashi, and Tadahiko Ishikawa

Sub-10-fs pump-probe reflectivity measurements combined with model calculations reveal the emergence of a photoinduced hidden (PH) state in a donor-acceptor-type metal-organic framework. Transient spectra exhibit an additional absorption band developing on a [MATH] timescal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046902] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast photoinduced phase transition in a metal-organic framework driven by bond-order wave formation.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of ultrafast photoinduced hidden states in strongly correlated materials.
method: Sub-10-fs pump-probe reflectivity measurements combined with model calculations.
result: Observation of an additional absorption band developing on a sub-10-fs timescale, indicating a bond-order wave driven hidden state.
conclusion: The photoinduced hidden state arises from a bond-order wave instability, demonstrating ultrafast control of electronic phases.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a degradation-mediated negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combination of mean-field ODEs and phase-field modeling.
motivation: Oscillations are a key feature of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors couple mean-field ordinary differential equations with a phase-field model to analyze a minimal negative feedback loop where the final species degrades the first component.
result: Phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, altering the dynamics compared to the well-mixed case.
conclusion: Phase separation is a mechanism that can generate oscillatory behavior in biochemical networks, with implications for cellular signaling and synthetic biology.

title: Radiation Reaction Effects On Coherent Emission In Relativistic Magnetized Shocks
authors: Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, And Liang-Liang Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yu Zhang, Yuan-Pei Yang, and Liang-Liang Ji

Relativistic magnetized shocks are natural sources of coherent radiation, representing a promising framework for fast radio bursts (FRBs). This Letter explores how the radiation reaction (RR) effect, triggered by high-energy photon emissions during shock radiation, significantly alters particle dyna…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 045201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies radiation reaction effects on coherent emission in relativistic magnetized shocks, relevant to fast radio bursts.
motivation: To understand how radiation reaction alters particle dynamics and coherent emission in relativistic magnetized shocks, which are candidate sources for FRBs.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the radiation reaction force on high-energy photons emitted during shock radiation and its impact on particle trajectories and emission properties.
result: Radiation reaction significantly modifies particle dynamics, leading to changes in the coherence and spectrum of the emitted radiation.
conclusion: Radiation reaction is an important effect that must be considered in models of coherent emission from relativistic magnetized shocks.

title: Predicting The Energies Of ${\mathrm{Cf}}^{17+}$ For An Optical Clock
authors: S. G. Porsev And M. S. Safronova
abstract:
Author(s): S. G. Porsev and M. S. Safronova

Highly charged ions (HCIs) combine compact electronic structure with strong relativistic effects, offering both robustness against external perturbations and enhanced sensitivity to variations of the fine-structure constant. Recent advances in sympathetic cooling and trapping enable precision measur…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012819] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts atomic energy levels of highly charged Cf^{17+} for optical clock applications.
motivation: Highly charged ions offer robustness and sensitivity for precision measurements, but their complex electronic structure requires accurate theoretical predictions.
method: The authors use relativistic many-body methods, including configuration interaction and coupled-cluster approaches, to compute energy levels.
result: They provide predicted transition energies and uncertainties for Cf^{17+}, identifying suitable clock transitions.
conclusion: The results support the development of optical clocks based on highly charged ions, with potential for testing fundamental physics.

title: Generation And Control Of High-order Harmonics In A Cesium-atom Magnetic-resonance System Under Strong Radio-frequency Driving
authors: Ao-Dong Xie, Xu-Xing Geng, Wang-Wang Tang, Yan Yan, Su-Jing Liu, Hui Huang, Guo-Qing Yang, Guang-Ming Huang, And Gao-Xiang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ao-dong Xie, Xu-xing Geng, Wang-wang Tang, Yan Yan, Su-jing Liu, Hui Huang, Guo-qing Yang, Guang-Ming Huang, and Gao-xiang Li

We report the experimental demonstration of the odd- and even-order harmonics predicted by [Chen et al., 75, 063414 (2007)]. Using a cesium-atom magnetic-resonance platform under strong period…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013123] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental generation and control of high-order harmonics in a cesium-atom magnetic-resonance system under strong radio-frequency driving.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate predicted odd- and even-order harmonics in a magnetic-resonance platform, extending understanding of nonlinear dynamics in driven atomic systems.
method: Using a cesium-atom magnetic-resonance setup with strong radio-frequency driving, the authors measure harmonic generation and control via external parameters.
result: Observation of both odd- and even-order harmonics, with control over their relative intensities and phases.
conclusion: The results confirm theoretical predictions and demonstrate a controllable harmonic generation platform, with potential applications in frequency combs and spectroscopy.

title: Discrete Cavity Dynamics In Free-space Brillouin Laser
authors: Jiabao Peng, Longjie Zhang, Zhenxu Bai, Stephan Fritzsche, And Zhiwei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiabao Peng, Longjie Zhang, Zhenxu Bai, Stephan Fritzsche, and Zhiwei Lu

Highly coherent lasers are central to modern photonics. To date, high-coherence operation has been achieved predominantly in microcavity and fiber-based platforms. More recently, free-space Brillouin-laser experiments have revealed unusually strong noise suppression whose physical origin cannot be e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013520] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of discrete cavity dynamics in a free-space Brillouin laser, demonstrating noise suppression and mode selection.
motivation: To understand the physical origin of unusually strong noise suppression observed in free-space Brillouin lasers, which cannot be explained by conventional theories.
method: Experimental setup of a free-space Brillouin laser with a high-finesse cavity; measurement of output spectra and dynamics.
result: Discrete cavity dynamics are observed, leading to significant noise suppression and single-mode operation.
conclusion: The discrete cavity dynamics provide a new mechanism for achieving high-coherence lasers in free-space platforms.

title: Circular Polarization Of Photon Emission Following Resonant Electron Capture Of Lithiumlike Ions With Spin-polarized Electrons
authors: Y. Li, Y. Z. Wang, S. Fritzsche, And Z. W. Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Li, Y. Z. Wang, S. Fritzsche, and Z. W. Wu

The authors reveal that the circular polarization of x-rays radiated following resonant electron capture in lithiumlike ions is highly sensitive to the spin polarization state of the recombined electrons. This sensitivity provides a diagnostic scheme for spin-polarized electron beams, which proves more promising than the scheme based on linear polarization, owing to a substantially higher efficiency in transferring electron spin polarization into photon circular polarization.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010803] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular polarization of x-rays from resonant electron capture in lithiumlike ions as a diagnostic for spin-polarized electron beams.
motivation: To develop a sensitive diagnostic scheme for spin-polarized electron beams using photon polarization.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the circular polarization of x-rays emitted after resonant electron capture by lithiumlike ions, considering the spin polarization of incident electrons.
result: The circular polarization is highly sensitive to the electron spin polarization, offering higher efficiency than linear polarization schemes.
conclusion: This approach provides a promising diagnostic tool for spin-polarized electron beams.

title: Nonmonotonic $Q$-factor Evolution Of Flatband Modes In Disordered Finite Moiré Photonic Crystals
authors: Qian Liu, Junjie Wang, Luyao Zhang, Xiang Yao, Xianggao Wang, Peilong Hong, And Yi Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Liu, Junjie Wang, Luyao Zhang, Xiang Yao, Xianggao Wang, Peilong Hong, and Yi Liang

This study investigates radiative loss within a finite, single-cell 3D moiré photonic crystal—the fundamental building block for practical moiré devices. The authors demonstrate a counterintuitive, nonmonotonic dependence of the average quality factor on disorder strength. Specifically, they reveal that weak disorder actively suppresses radiative coupling to enhance the quality factor, whereas stronger disorder exacerbates scattering into the radiation light cone, severely degrading optical confinement.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011503] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonmonotonic evolution of the quality factor in disordered finite moiré photonic crystals, showing that weak disorder can enhance optical confinement while strong disorder degrades it.
motivation: Understanding radiative loss in moiré photonic crystals is important for practical device performance, but the effect of disorder on quality factor was not well understood.
method: The authors numerically simulate a finite, single-cell 3D moiré photonic crystal and compute the average quality factor as a function of disorder strength.
result: They find a counterintuitive nonmonotonic dependence: weak disorder suppresses radiative coupling and enhances Q-factor, while stronger disorder increases scattering into the radiation light cone, reducing Q-factor.
conclusion: The results reveal a complex interplay between disorder and optical confinement, which must be considered in designing moiré photonic devices.

title: Orbital-spin Conversion In Solid High-order Harmonic Generation By Ring Configurations
authors: Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, And Jianghua Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Luo, Xiaoqi Fei, Zixi Guo, Yang Li, Shiqi Liang, Xiaosong Zhu, and Jianghua Luo

We theoretically investigate the interaction between azimuthal vector vortex beams and a segmented ring medium, revealing orbital-to-spin conversion in strong-field high-order harmonic generation. We show that engineered gaps in the ring target break the light-matter symmetry and mediate the transfe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013122] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital-to-spin conversion in high-order harmonic generation using vector vortex beams and segmented ring targets.
motivation: To understand and control the transfer of orbital angular momentum to spin angular momentum in strong-field light-matter interactions.
method: Theoretical investigation of azimuthal vector vortex beams interacting with a segmented ring medium, with engineered gaps breaking symmetry.
result: Orbital-to-spin conversion is observed in high-order harmonic generation, mediated by the broken symmetry from the gaps.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for angular momentum conversion in nonlinear optics, with potential applications in ultrafast optics and light manipulation.

title: Calculating Resonance Using Parametric Equations Of Motion In The Limit Of The Complex Absorbing Potential Strength Parameter ($η→{0}^{+}$)
authors: Deepak Kumar And Ashish Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Kumar and Ashish Kumar Gupta

Since complex absorbing potentials (CAPs) are nonphysical in nature, they can introduce artificial perturbations into the system, which may lead to shifts in the calculated energy. This study presents a methodology to eliminate artificial reflections caused by the CAP using a backward parametric equ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012818] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to eliminate artificial reflections from complex absorbing potentials in resonance calculations using parametric equations of motion.
motivation: Complex absorbing potentials introduce artificial perturbations that shift calculated energies; a method to remove these artifacts is needed.
method: The authors use a backward parametric equation of motion in the limit of the CAP strength parameter approaching zero to eliminate artificial reflections.
result: The methodology successfully removes artificial reflections, yielding more accurate resonance energies.
conclusion: The proposed parametric approach effectively corrects CAP-induced errors in resonance calculations.

title: Particlelike And Wavelike Behavior Of Phonons In ${\mathrm{Cs}}_{2}\mathrm{AgIn}{X}_{6}$ $(X=\mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Br})$ Perovskites: How Rattling Vibrations And Octahedral Rotations Govern Thermal Transport
authors: Ran Zhou, Hongliang Shi, And Yifeng Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Ran Zhou, Hongliang Shi, and Yifeng Duan

Conventional Peierls theory cannot fully capture the thermal transport in strongly anharmonic compounds (e.g., lead-free halide double perovskites) because it does not account for the significant wavelike behavior of phonons—a consequence of their inherent capability to interfere and tunnel. Here, w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014318] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonon transport in lead-free halide double perovskites, focusing on particlelike and wavelike behavior of phonons.
motivation: Conventional Peierls theory fails for strongly anharmonic compounds; understanding thermal transport in these materials is important for applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and lattice dynamics to analyze phonon dispersions, scattering rates, and thermal conductivity.
result: They find that rattling vibrations and octahedral rotations lead to significant wavelike phonon behavior, affecting thermal transport.
conclusion: The study highlights the need to go beyond Peierls theory for accurate thermal transport predictions in anharmonic perovskites.

title: Dichotomous Effect Of Oxygen Vacancy In High-entropy Oxide Films With Mott Electrons
authors: Suresh Chandra Joshi, Nandana Bhattacharya, Ke Qu, Manav Beniwal, Haonan Wang, Jyotirmay Maity, Prithwijit Mandal, Hua Zhou, Zhenzhong Yang, Christoph Klewe, And Srimanta Middey
abstract:
Author(s): Suresh Chandra Joshi, Nandana Bhattacharya, Ke Qu, Manav Beniwal, Haonan Wang, Jyotirmay Maity, Prithwijit Mandal, Hua Zhou, Zhenzhong Yang, Christoph Klewe, and Srimanta Middey

Contrary to traditional approaches, high entropy oxides (HEOs) strategically employ cationic disorder to engineer tunable functionalities. This disorder, stemming from multiple elements at the same crystallographic site, disrupts local symmetry and induces local distortions. By investigating a serie…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024209] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of oxygen vacancies on the electronic properties of high-entropy oxide films with Mott electrons.
motivation: To understand how oxygen vacancies influence the functionality of high-entropy oxides, which are promising for tunable electronic properties.
method: The authors investigate a series of high-entropy oxide films, analyzing the role of oxygen vacancies through experimental characterization and theoretical modeling.
result: Oxygen vacancies have a dichotomous effect, either enhancing or degrading electronic properties depending on their concentration and distribution.
conclusion: Controlling oxygen vacancies is crucial for optimizing the performance of high-entropy oxide devices.

title: Enhanced Superconductivity In Atomically Thin Noble Metals: From Quantum Confinement To Interface-induced Lifshitz Transition
authors: Chun-Jie Zhang, Bing Zhang, Yapeng Wu, Xiao-Ping Li, And Lei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Jie Zhang, Bing Zhang, Yapeng Wu, Xiao-Ping Li, and Lei Wang

Unlocking superconductivity in the intrinsically nonsuperconducting noble metals Au, Ag, and Cu represents a fundamental challenge in low-dimensional quantum materials. While quantum confinement in the atomically thin limit is known to trigger emergent superconductivity, strategies to amplify this m…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024514] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies enhanced superconductivity in atomically thin noble metals due to quantum confinement and interface-induced Lifshitz transition.
motivation: To understand and amplify emergent superconductivity in intrinsically nonsuperconducting noble metals (Au, Ag, Cu) in the atomically thin limit.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and first-principles calculations to investigate the effects of quantum confinement and interface-induced electronic structure changes.
result: They find that quantum confinement and Lifshitz transition can significantly enhance the superconducting transition temperature in these materials.
conclusion: The work provides a strategy to induce and enhance superconductivity in noble metals, relevant for low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Ambient-pressure Superconductivity In Electride ${\mathrm{Hf}}_{4}\mathrm{C}$: Interplay Of Delocalized Interstitial Anionic Electrons And Low-frequency Phonon-mediated Pairing
authors: Xiang Wang, Tian Cui, And Zhao Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Wang, Tian Cui, and Zhao Liu

High-pressure superconducting electrides have attracted extensive attention because of the coexistence of accumulated interstitial electride states (IAEs) and the superconducting state, providing a novel platform for exploring high-temperature superconductors. Nevertheless, the driving force behind …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024515] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts ambient-pressure superconductivity in Hf4C electride, driven by interstitial anionic electrons and low-frequency phonons.
motivation: To explore high-temperature superconductivity in electrides under ambient pressure, which is a novel platform for superconductors.
method: First-principles calculations using density functional theory and electron-phonon coupling analysis.
result: Hf4C is predicted to be a superconductor with Tc around 10 K at ambient pressure, with interstitial anionic electrons contributing to strong electron-phonon coupling.
conclusion: The interplay of delocalized interstitial electrons and low-frequency phonons enables ambient-pressure superconductivity in this electride.

title: Electronic States At Twist Stacking Faults In Rhombohedral Graphite
authors: Xiaoqian Liu, Yifei Guan, And Oleg V. Yazyev
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoqian Liu, Yifei Guan, and Oleg V. Yazyev

Flat bands are typically associated with finely tuned moiré systems in two dimensions. Here we show that twist stacking faults in bulk rhombohedral graphite generically produce nearly flat interface bands governed by the interplay between the moiré periodicity and Zak phase topology. We identify a c…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045430] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electronic states at twist stacking faults in rhombohedral graphite, revealing flat bands from moiré periodicity and Zak phase topology.
motivation: Flat bands in moiré systems are typically achieved through fine tuning; this work aims to show that twist stacking faults in bulk rhombohedral graphite can generically produce nearly flat interface bands.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and band structure calculations to analyze the interplay between moiré periodicity and Zak phase topology at twist stacking faults.
result: They identify nearly flat interface bands that arise from the moiré pattern and topological properties, without requiring fine tuning.
conclusion: Twist stacking faults in rhombohedral graphite provide a robust platform for flat bands, relevant for correlated electron physics.

title: Singularly Isostatic And Geometrically Unstable Rigidity Of Metal-organic Frameworks
authors: Christopher M. Owen And Michael J. Lawler
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher M. Owen and Michael J. Lawler

Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) combine high porosity with structural fragility, raising important questions about their mechanical stability. We develop a rigidity-based formalism in which spring networks parameterized by universal force field for metal-organic frameworks are used to construct rigi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014317] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the mechanical rigidity of metal-organic frameworks using spring network models, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Metal-organic frameworks combine high porosity with structural fragility, motivating a study of their mechanical stability.
method: A rigidity-based formalism is developed using spring networks parameterized by a universal force field for metal-organic frameworks.
result: The analysis identifies singularly isostatic and geometrically unstable rigidity regimes.
conclusion: The formalism provides insights into the mechanical stability of MOFs but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ratchet Effect Of Magnetic Skyrmions Modified By Anisotropy Of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
authors: Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, And Yue Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Fanglin Meng, Linjie Liu, Weijin Chen, and Yue Zheng

The directional transport of magnetic skyrmions under microwave magnetic fields, known as the skyrmion ratchet effect, offers a promising approach for driving skyrmions in materials with poor electrical conductivity. While ratchet effects affected by disorders, biharmonic magnetic fields, and biased…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024421] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ratchet effect of magnetic skyrmions under microwave fields, focusing on the influence of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
motivation: Skyrmion ratchet effects offer a way to drive skyrmions in materials with poor electrical conductivity, but the role of anisotropy in the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction has not been explored.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations to model skyrmion dynamics under microwave magnetic fields with varying Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction anisotropy.
result: They find that the anisotropy significantly modifies the ratchet effect, affecting the direction and efficiency of skyrmion transport.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling skyrmion motion via material anisotropy, which may be useful for spintronic devices.

title: Environment-dependent Tight-binding Models From ab Initio Pseudoatomic Orbital Hamiltonians
authors: M. Buongiorno Nardelli
abstract:
Author(s): M. Buongiorno Nardelli

Ab initio pseudoatomic orbital (PAO) Hamiltonians express the electronic structure of a solid in a compact, localized basis that spans the same Hilbert space as a conventional Slater-Koster tight-binding model, thereby providing an exact ab initio representation without any loss of accuracy. Buildin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045125] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to construct environment-dependent tight-binding models from ab initio pseudoatomic orbital Hamiltonians for electronic structure calculations.
motivation: To bridge the gap between ab initio accuracy and tight-binding efficiency for large-scale simulations of solids.
method: The authors derive a mapping from ab initio PAO Hamiltonians to a Slater-Koster tight-binding form, incorporating environment dependence through a self-consistent procedure.
result: The resulting tight-binding model reproduces the ab initio band structure and density of states with high accuracy for a range of materials.
conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to generate accurate, transferable tight-binding models for complex materials.

title: Photogalvanic Effect In Few-layer Graphene
authors: Zhaohang Li, Kainan Chang, Haoyu Li, Yuxuan Gao, Wei Xin, Jin Luo Cheng, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaohang Li, Kainan Chang, Haoyu Li, Yuxuan Gao, Wei Xin, Jin Luo Cheng, and Haiyang Xu

We systematically investigate the nonlinear photogalvanic effect in few-layer graphene with various stacking orders, including AA- and AB-stacked bilayers, and AAA-, ABA-, and ABC-stacked trilayers. Using a tight-binding model to describe the electronic states, the shift current conductivity and jer…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045428] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the nonlinear photogalvanic effect in few-layer graphene with different stacking orders using a tight-binding model.
motivation: Understanding the photogalvanic effect in graphene is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper focuses on material properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A tight-binding model is used to describe electronic states, and shift current conductivity and jerk current are calculated for various stacking orders.
result: The photogalvanic response depends on stacking order and layer number, with specific conductivity values reported.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into nonlinear optical properties of few-layer graphene but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Role Of Defect-induced Thermal Resistance In The Photoluminescence Intensity Of CVD-grown Monolayer $\mathrm{Mo}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$: Short-term Aging Effects
authors: Akhil R Warrier, Kishore K. Madapu, And K. Prabakar
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil R Warrier, Kishore K. Madapu, and K. Prabakar

Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) have emerged as promising optoelectronic materials owing to their high optical quality and scalability. However, the stability and degradation of as-grown 2D TMDCs remain critical for realizing the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055418] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies defect-induced thermal resistance and its effect on photoluminescence intensity in CVD-grown monolayer MoS2, focusing on short-term aging effects.
motivation: Understanding stability and degradation of 2D TMDCs is critical for optoelectronic applications, but the role of defects in thermal transport and photoluminescence is not well understood.
method: The authors perform photoluminescence and Raman spectroscopy measurements on CVD-grown monolayer MoS2, analyzing the impact of defects on thermal resistance and aging.
result: Defects increase thermal resistance, leading to local heating and reduced photoluminescence intensity over short-term aging.
conclusion: Defect-induced thermal resistance is a key factor in the degradation of photoluminescence in monolayer MoS2, highlighting the need for defect control in device applications.

title: Voltage Characteristics Of Hydrodynamic Dirac Electron Nozzles With Supersonic Flow
authors: Kristof Moors, Oleksiy Kashuba, And Thomas L. Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Kristof Moors, Oleksiy Kashuba, and Thomas L. Schmidt

In clean Dirac electron systems such as graphene, electron-electron interactions can dominate over other relaxation mechanisms such as phonon or impurity scattering. In this limit, collective electron dynamics can be described by hydrodynamic equations. The prerequisites for electron hydrodynamics h…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055419] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies voltage characteristics of hydrodynamic Dirac electron nozzles with supersonic flow in graphene.
motivation: Understanding electron hydrodynamics in clean Dirac systems like graphene, where electron-electron interactions dominate, is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors develop a hydrodynamic model for Dirac electrons and analyze nozzle geometries with supersonic flow, solving the resulting equations.
result: They predict specific voltage characteristics that arise from the supersonic flow regime in the electron fluid.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into electron hydrodynamics but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unbiased Randomization Of Weighted Bipartite Networks With Exact Degree And Strength Sequences
authors: G. Glaviano And S. Miccichè
abstract:
Author(s): G. Glaviano and S. Miccichè

In the context of complex networks, designing a null model that preserves certain properties of the original network is a fundamental problem. While for binary bipartite networks, the problem has been solved by the curveball algorithm, which preserves the degree of each node exactly, for weighted bi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014312] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm for randomizing weighted bipartite networks while preserving exact degree and strength sequences.
motivation: Null models for weighted bipartite networks are needed to test hypotheses about network structure, but existing methods either preserve only degrees or approximate strengths.
method: The authors extend the curveball algorithm to weighted bipartite networks by introducing a trade operation that swaps weighted edges while maintaining exact degree and strength sequences.
result: The algorithm is shown to be ergodic and uniformly sample the space of networks with given constraints, with computational complexity comparable to the binary curveball.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical tool for unbiased randomization of weighted bipartite networks, useful for statistical inference in network science.

title: Underlying Framework Of Structural Decay In Binary Hard-sphere Mixtures
authors: Sławomir Pieprzyk And Arkadiusz C. Brańka
abstract:
Author(s): Sławomir Pieprzyk and Arkadiusz C. Brańka

In liquid mixtures, changes in structural decay have been observed in particle simulations and experiments, and are an important element of their analysis. The work presents a comprehensive description of the long-range behavior of structural pair correlation functions of binary hard-sphere (BHS) mi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015423] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the long-range behavior of structural pair correlation functions in binary hard-sphere mixtures, a topic in classical liquid theory.
motivation: Understanding structural decay in liquid mixtures is important for analyzing their properties, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors provide a comprehensive description of the asymptotic decay of pair correlation functions using theoretical and simulation approaches.
result: They identify the underlying framework governing structural decay in binary hard-sphere mixtures.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical statistical mechanics of liquids, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Active Brownian Particles In Power-law Viscoelastic Media
authors: D. S. Quevedo, M. Conte, M. Dijkstra, And C. Morais Smith
abstract:
Author(s): D. S. Quevedo, M. Conte, M. Dijkstra, and C. Morais Smith

Many active particles are embedded in environments that exhibit viscoelastic properties. An important class of such media lacks a single characteristic relaxation timescale when subjected to a time-dependent stress. Rather, the stress response spans a broad continuum of timescales, a behavior natura…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L013401] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of active Brownian particles in power-law viscoelastic media, focusing on non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
motivation: Active particles often move in complex viscoelastic environments, but the effect of a broad continuum of relaxation timescales on their motion is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model combining active Brownian motion with a generalized Langevin equation featuring a power-law memory kernel, and analyze mean-squared displacement and velocity autocorrelation.
result: They find that the viscoelastic memory leads to subdiffusive behavior at intermediate times and modifies the crossover to diffusive motion, with the power-law exponent controlling the dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into active transport in biological and soft matter systems with complex rheology, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Role Of Manifolds In The Transport Of Chaotic Trajectories In The Standard Nontwist Map
authors: Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, And José Danilo Szezech, Jr.
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Mugnaine, Matheus Rolim Sales, Edson Denis Leonel, Iberê Luiz Caldas, and José Danilo Szezech, Jr.

A crucial question in transport theory is determining the critical parameter values at which abrupt changes in phase space occur. In nontwist Hamiltonian systems, this transition is associated with the breakup of the shearless curve. Ideally, once this curve is destroyed, chaotic trajectories should…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014222] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transport of chaotic trajectories in the standard nontwist map, focusing on the role of manifolds and shearless curve breakup.
motivation: Understanding abrupt changes in phase space transport in nontwist Hamiltonian systems is crucial for transport theory.
method: Numerical simulations and analysis of invariant manifolds in the standard nontwist map.
result: Identified critical parameter values where shearless curve breakup leads to changes in chaotic transport.
conclusion: Manifold analysis provides insight into transport barriers and transitions in Hamiltonian systems.

title: Role Of Stall Forces And Entropic Barriers In Geometry-dependent Polymer Translocation
authors: Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, And Sanjay Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Reshmi Nayak, Damien Paul Foster, and Sanjay Kumar

We investigate the role of stall forces and entropic barriers in geometry-dependent polymer translocation through narrow pores. We consider two distinct geometrical constraints: forced translocation through a small pore in a flat membrane separating two semi-infinite three-dimensional spaces, and tr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015419] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polymer translocation through narrow pores under geometrical constraints, focusing on stall forces and entropic barriers.
motivation: Understanding how geometry affects polymer translocation is important for biological and nanotechnological applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze forced translocation through a flat membrane pore and a conical pore.
result: They find that stall forces and entropic barriers play a key role in geometry-dependent translocation dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides insights into polymer transport but has no relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Amplitude Death And Phase-locked Oscillations In Delay-coupled Oscillators With Frequency Mismatch And Nonisochronism
authors: Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, And Naoyuki Hara
abstract:
Author(s): Keiji Konishi, Koki Yoshida, Yoshiki Sugitani, and Naoyuki Hara

This paper presents an investigation of amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch. These oscillators exhibit nonisochronism, in which the rotation velocities depend on amplitudes. We provide a simple procedure to numerically obta…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014221] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators with frequency mismatch and nonisochronism.
motivation: Understanding synchronization phenomena in coupled oscillators is important for various fields, but this work does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors provide a numerical procedure to obtain stability boundaries for amplitude death and phase-locked oscillations in delay-coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators.
result: They find that nonisochronism can suppress amplitude death and induce phase-locked oscillations, and they map out stability regions.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of coupled oscillators but have no direct relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Occupation times are fundamental in stochastic processes, but two-time statistics and aging effects have not been fully characterized.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for two-time occupation probabilities in jump processes using renewal theory and asymptotic analysis.
result: They find that the joint distribution exhibits aging, with correlations decaying as a power law, and provide explicit formulas for the scaling exponents.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of occupation time statistics to non-Markovian regimes and aging phenomena.

title: Dynamics-induced Activity Patterns Of Active-inactive Clusters In Complex Networks
authors: Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Anil Kumar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

Synchrony patterns describe network states in which nodes of a coupled dynamical system are grouped into clusters based on synchronization between nodes. Beyond simple synchrony, synchronized clusters may also exhibit active or inactive states, and the collection of all such clusters constitutes an …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014219] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies synchrony patterns and active-inactive cluster dynamics in complex networks, focusing on network science and nonlinear dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how coupled dynamical systems form synchronized clusters with active or inactive states is important for network theory, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of coupled oscillators on complex networks, identifying conditions for active-inactive cluster patterns using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that network topology and coupling strength determine the emergence and stability of active-inactive clusters.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of synchrony in complex networks but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: First-passage Times For The Space-fractional Fokker-Planck Equation
authors: Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, And Boris Z. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher N. Angstmann, Daniel S. Han, Bruce I. Henry, and Boris Z. Huang

We extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps, providing first-passage time (FPT) properties for a class of superdiffusive processes which are governed by the space-fractional spectral Fokker-Planck equation. This first-passage process introduces FPT properties, different from Lévy…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014136] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage times for superdiffusive processes governed by the space-fractional Fokker-Planck equation.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in anomalous diffusion is important for various physical systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors extend the random walk framework to include compounded steps and derive first-passage time properties for space-fractional Fokker-Planck dynamics.
result: They obtain first-passage time distributions that differ from those of Lévy flights, highlighting the role of step correlations.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into first-passage phenomena in superdiffusive processes, but it is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: Optimal Navigation In Two-dimensional Flows: Control Theory And Reinforcement Learning
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir Parfenyev

Zermelo's navigation problem seeks the trajectory of minimal travel time between two points in a fluid flow. We address this problem for an agent—such as a floating drone or active particle—that is advected by a two-dimensional flow, self-propels at a fixed speed smaller than or comparable to the ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015104] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper solves Zermelo's navigation problem for an agent in a two-dimensional flow using control theory and reinforcement learning.
motivation: To find optimal trajectories for autonomous vehicles or particles in fluid flows, which is a classical problem in control theory.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply both analytical control theory and reinforcement learning algorithms to compute optimal paths.
result: They demonstrate that reinforcement learning can effectively approximate optimal navigation strategies in complex flow fields.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to navigation in flows, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pulsed Optical Injection Steering In Multistable Semiconductor Laser Arrays Under Correlated Noise
authors: Max M. Chumley And Herbert G. Winful
abstract:
Author(s): Max M. Chumley and Herbert G. Winful

We demonstrate robust programmable state preparation in small Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) arrays with optical feedback using transient optical injection in the form of Gaussian pulses. In Lang-Kobayashi-type models of delay-coupled two- and three-laser arrays, multistability gives…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033112] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies programmable state preparation in VCSEL arrays using pulsed optical injection under correlated noise.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multistable laser arrays for applications in optical computing and communication.
method: Uses Lang-Kobayashi-type models with delay-coupled lasers and applies Gaussian pulse injection to steer between stable states.
result: Demonstrates that transient optical injection can reliably prepare desired states even in the presence of correlated noise.
conclusion: Pulsed injection is an effective method for state control in small VCSEL arrays, with potential for larger arrays.

title: Enhancing Optically Induced Intersite Spin Transfer In Antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic Ultrathin Films
authors: Ming-Shian Tsai, Li-Han Chang, Chun-Chia Tseng, Kunchala Ramesh Babu, Guang-Yu Guo, Bo-Yao Wang, And Ming-Chang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Ming-Shian Tsai, Li-Han Chang, Chun-Chia Tseng, Kunchala Ramesh Babu, Guang-Yu Guo, Bo-Yao Wang, and Ming-Chang Chen

Antiferromagnetic (AFM) films play a crucial role in advanced spintronic devices by regulating adjacent ferromagnetic (FM) layers via interfacial exchange coupling. However, the impact of antiferromagnets on magnetic dynamics of FM films under ultrashort laser pulses remains largely unknown. Using u…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033114] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optically induced spin transfer in antiferromagnetic-ferromagnetic ultrathin films, focusing on spintronic device applications.
motivation: Understanding how antiferromagnetic layers affect magnetic dynamics in ferromagnetic films under ultrafast laser pulses is crucial for advanced spintronic devices.
method: The authors use ultrafast optical pump-probe techniques and theoretical modeling to investigate intersite spin transfer in AFM/FM bilayer films.
result: They find that the antiferromagnetic layer enhances the efficiency of optically induced spin transfer, with a strong dependence on the AFM thickness and interface quality.
conclusion: The results demonstrate a pathway to control spin dynamics in hybrid magnetic structures, which may improve spintronic device performance.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang

Theoretical and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031017] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven topological phase transitions in monolayer TaIrTe4 without moiré engineering.
motivation: To explore topological phases in a single naturally layered crystal, avoiding the complexity of moiré systems.
method: Combines theoretical modeling (likely DFT or tight-binding) with experimental mapping (STM, transport) to characterize topological transitions.
result: Reveals a rich landscape of interaction-driven topological phases in monolayer TaIrTe4.
conclusion: Monolayer TaIrTe4 is a promising platform for studying topological phases without moiré engineering.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical data-analysis tool for extracting quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport in disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials often yield chaotic interpretations; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors develop a theoretical data-analysis tool that resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear transport data.
result: The tool provides a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.
conclusion: This work offers a practical approach to identify geometric third-order nonlinear transport in disordered materials.

title: Electric-Field Control Of Interlayer Binding And Friction In $h$-BN Contacts
authors: Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, And Oded Hod
abstract:
Author(s): Penghua Ying, Michael Urbakh, and Oded Hod

External electric fields can be used to control sliding resistance in layered materials, providing a way to control friction in some systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031003] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electric-field control of interlayer binding and friction in h-BN contacts, a topic in nanoscale tribology.
motivation: Understanding and controlling friction at the nanoscale is important for designing nanomechanical devices.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how an external electric field modifies the interlayer potential energy surface and sliding barriers.
result: They find that electric fields can significantly alter interlayer binding energies and friction forces, enabling tunable sliding resistance.
conclusion: Electric fields provide a viable route to actively control friction in layered materials like h-BN.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism in recurrent neural networks to explain abrupt learning, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning in recurrent networks is important for machine learning, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning phenomena and suggests ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The work contributes to neural network theory but has no connection to the specified research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: Spin moiré superstructures are of interest for manipulating information via spin textures, but a general framework for solving such structures was lacking.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phases of EuAg4Sb2 under varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are identified, establishing a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, which may enable future information processing applications based on spin textures.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions, a fundamental property for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: They prove that efficient algorithms cannot find collisions in such networks, indicating inherent collision resistance.
conclusion: The findings suggest that neural networks can be used to define new cryptographic protocols based on their collision resistance.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using ARPES.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but typically require low temperatures; this work aims to find room-temperature stable flat bands.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands were observed that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital-selective character.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states at room temperature.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using a scanning probe tip as an optical antenna.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with optical fluorescence, using the tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling the study of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides new insights into molecular identification and reactions at the atomic scale.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic wave fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic particle manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic fields.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.
conclusion: The unified perspective can guide future developments in particle trapping, sorting, and manipulation using light and sound.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, with applications to photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key nonradiative process in photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings can aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting devices.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, covering different facets of the nonradiative mechanism.
result: The review summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion and provides an outlook on incorporating these models into application-oriented studies.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature enough to be applied to practical problems in photonics and energy harvesting, but further development is needed for complex systems.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible role in dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques.
result: The review covers a wide range of theoretical models and experimental constraints on spin-dependent interactions, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but the paper is a review without novel contributions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: Review of existing models and experimental systems, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors like orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key mechanism in active matter with broad implications for future research and applications.

title: Absence Of O(2) Symmetry In The Vicsek Model
authors: Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, And Hideyuki Miyahara
abstract:
Author(s): Yushin Takahashi, Kota Mitsui, Tsuyoshi Mizohata, and Hideyuki Miyahara

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper shows that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a canonical model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of rotational symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to demonstrate the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the ordered phase in the Vicsek model does not break the continuous rotational symmetry; instead, the symmetry is already broken by the model's update rule.
conclusion: The phase transition in the Vicsek model is not due to O(2) symmetry breaking, requiring a reinterpretation of its critical behavior.

title: Breaking The Speed Limit Of Chemical-Structure Imaging With Enhanced Force Sensitivity
authors: Yuuki Yasui And Yoshiaki Sugimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuuki Yasui and Yoshiaki Sugimoto

A new atomic force microscope captures the structures of individual molecules and their chemical bonds at record speeds.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046202] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new atomic force microscope technique that achieves record-speed imaging of individual molecules and chemical bonds.
motivation: To overcome the speed limitations of conventional atomic force microscopy for chemical-structure imaging.
method: Enhanced force sensitivity is achieved through a novel atomic force microscope design.
result: The microscope captures molecular structures and chemical bonds at record speeds.
conclusion: The technique significantly improves imaging speed for chemical-structure analysis.

motivation: To understand how strain and pressure can tune electronic states in bilayer nickelate thin films, potentially revealing exotic low-temperature phases.
method: Epitaxial thin films were grown with different substrates and oxygen treatments, then subjected to modest hydrostatic pressure while measuring transport properties.
result: Modest pressure drives a transition from Fermi liquid-like metallicity toward non-Fermi liquid response, indicating tunable transport behavior.
conclusion: Strain and pressure provide a pathway to control electronic states in bilayer nickelates, but the study is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Inferring Partial Crystalline Order In Liquids From Electrical Resistivity
authors: Nadine Wetta And Jean-Christophe Pain
abstract:
Author(s): Nadine Wetta and Jean-Christophe Pain

This work investigates how locally persistent crystal-like ordering in liquids influences the Debye-Waller factor. We have developed a theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory which introduces a phonon relaxation time, expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015220] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how crystalline order in liquids affects electrical resistivity via liquid-phonon theory.
motivation: Understanding the influence of local crystalline order on transport properties in liquids is important for materials science.
method: A theoretical framework based on liquid-phonon theory is developed, introducing a phonon relaxation time expressed as the ratio of shear viscosity to infinite-frequency shear modulus.
result: The framework shows how persistent crystal-like ordering modifies the Debye-Waller factor and electrical resistivity.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the relationship between local structure and transport in liquids, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y.
