Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using ARPES.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Understanding transplutonium materials is important for nuclear power and waste management, and their unique 5f electron behavior under pressure is of fundamental interest.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It highlights the challenges and recent progress in studying these radioactive materials, revealing complex electronic behavior at the boundary between localized and itinerant electrons.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview of the field, but does not present new results or directly relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is important for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave signals (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to theoretical predictions of the nuclear equation of state.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized, showing consistency with nuclear physics calculations at lower densities but remaining uncertainties at higher densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state and our understanding of dense matter.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the review aims to summarize three complementary real-space techniques.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined approaches.
result: The review highlights how these techniques provide direct access to atomic-scale disorder in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Combining multiple real-space probes yields a more complete picture of defects, which is important for semiconductor materials science.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating all data up to the end of 2022.
result: A new set of self-consistent values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the most accurate and reliable set of fundamental constants, superseding previous versions.

title: Testing Local Lorentz Invariance With Laser Tracking Of The Lageos And Lageos Ii Satellites
authors: David Lucchesi, Massimo Visco, Roberto Peron, José C. Rodriguez, Massimo Bassan, Giuseppe Pucacco, Luciano Anselmo, Graham Appleby, Marco Cinelli, Alessandro Di Marco, Marco Lucente, Carmelo Magnafico, Carmen Pardini, And Feliciana Sapio
abstract:
Author(s): David Lucchesi, Massimo Visco, Roberto Peron, José C. Rodriguez, Massimo Bassan, Giuseppe Pucacco, Luciano Anselmo, Graham Appleby, Marco Cinelli, Alessandro Di Marco, Marco Lucente, Carmelo Magnafico, Carmen Pardini, and Feliciana Sapio (SaToR-G Collaboration)

Violations of Lorentz invariance, a cornerstone of modern physics, are predicted by theories of quantum gravity and by extensions of general relativity involving new vector or tensor fields. In the weak-field limit, such a violation would primarily manifest as a nonzero value for the post-Newtonian …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051401] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper tests local Lorentz invariance using laser tracking of LAGEOS satellites, finding no violation.
motivation: Lorentz invariance violations are predicted by quantum gravity and extensions of general relativity; testing them provides experimental constraints.
method: Analyzed laser ranging data from LAGEOS and LAGEOS II satellites to search for anomalous orbital precessions that would indicate Lorentz violation.
result: No evidence of Lorentz violation was found, setting new upper limits on post-Newtonian parameters.
conclusion: The results are consistent with Lorentz invariance, further constraining possible deviations from general relativity.

title: Direct Measurement Of The In-Medium ${η}^{′}$ Mass Spectrum Through The $γγ$ Decay Channel

abstract:

We measured the invariant mass of the [MATH] meson through the [MATH] decay channel to search for possible character change of [MATH] in a nuclear medium. The measured invariant-mass spectra were analyzed by fitting realistic spectral functions. An enhancement was observed in the lo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051901] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper measures the in-medium mass spectrum of the η′ meson via its γγ decay channel in nuclear matter.
motivation: To search for possible character change of the η′ meson in a nuclear medium, which is a topic in nuclear physics.
method: The invariant mass of the η′ meson was measured through the γγ decay channel, and the spectra were analyzed by fitting realistic spectral functions.
result: An enhancement was observed in the low-mass region of the invariant-mass spectra.
conclusion: The results provide direct measurement of the in-medium η′ mass spectrum, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Flow Through Bottlenecks: Stronger Is Slower
authors: Marta Grasa, Laciel Alonso-Llanes, Angel Garcimartín, And Iker Zuriguel
abstract:
Author(s): Marta Grasa, Laciel Alonso-Llanes, Angel Garcimartín, and Iker Zuriguel

We present experimental results of the flow of programmable robots through a bottleneck. With these agents, velocity and force can be decoupled—a unique feature allowing us to show that, in the absence of physical contact and pushing from behind, and despite the development of clogs, moving faster a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 058301] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: Experiments with programmable robots show that moving faster through a bottleneck increases clogging, contradicting intuition.
motivation: To understand the effect of agent speed on flow through bottlenecks in the absence of physical contact and pushing.
method: Programmable robots with decoupled velocity and force are used to measure flow and clogging at different speeds.
result: Faster movement leads to more frequent and longer clogs, reducing overall flow rate.
conclusion: In systems without pushing, increasing speed can be counterproductive for throughput.

title: Valley-Engineered Landau Polaritons In A Van Der Waals Semiconductor Microcavity
authors: Xinyue Zhang, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Song Luo, Long Xu, Xin Li, Yuquan Zhou, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Zhao Xu, Haodong Cheng, Long Zhang, And Zhanghai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyue Zhang, Hongming Zhang, Yaofeng Zhu, Hang Zhou, Song Luo, Long Xu, Xin Li, Yuquan Zhou, Yan Liu, Zheng Lv, Yuxin Duan, Zhao Xu, Haodong Cheng, Long Zhang, and Zhanghai Chen

Integrating a WSe

tldr: This paper studies valley-engineered Landau polaritons in a WSe2 monolayer microcavity, focusing on light-matter coupling and valley control.

tldr: This paper presents a quantum statistical method to predict dislocation mobility in high-entropy alloys without driven molecular dynamics.
motivation: Dislocation mobility in concentrated alloys is typically extracted from costly driven molecular dynamics simulations, motivating a more efficient approach.
method: The authors integrate out phonons on the Keldysh contour to obtain a causal memory kernel, whose zero-frequency limit gives the phonon drag coefficient.
result: The drag coefficient varies non-monotonically with composition, and effective medium estimates underpredict drag by about 2 to 8 due to a positive variance term.
conclusion: The equilibrium lattice dynamics approach provides a predictive and efficient alternative to driven molecular dynamics for dislocation mobility in high-entropy alloys.

abstract:

When subjected to vibrations, the effective viscosity of a granular medium depends heavily on both confining pressure and vibration parameters. In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but a unified framework reconciling experimental observations is lacking.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense vibrated granular flows.
result: Confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations of granular rheology under vibrations.

result: Mild tension with large optical depth values, consistent with Planck satellite measurements.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, a subset of nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the authors aim to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The paper reviews the history of the field, proposes a definition, and surveys recent topics including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
result: A clear definition of active matter is provided, distinguishing it from other nonequilibrium systems.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems with diverse applications, but it does not directly relate to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy emission from the Galactic Center, covering the supermassive black hole, compact sources, and plasma bubbles.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of the high-energy phenomena in the Galactic Center region.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths, including X-ray, gamma-ray, and radio observations.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of the quiescent and flaring emission from Sgr A*, the presence of plasma bubbles and chimneys, and the interaction with the surrounding molecular zone.
conclusion: The Galactic Center is a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysical processes, with many open questions remaining.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation and evolution.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: Recent advances provide a coherent understanding of vacuum breakdown, which can inform the design of more reliable high-power technologies and advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into quantum chromodynamics, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII, highlighting recent high-precision data from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Continued experimental studies of open-charm meson pairs will advance our understanding of strong interaction dynamics and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its legacy in planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the Arecibo Observatory's contributions and impact on various scientific fields.
method: The editorial presents three colloquia that review the observatory's achievements.
result: The paper highlights Arecibo's revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has left a lasting legacy in multiple areas of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of solar system bodies and near-Earth asteroids.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information that complements in-situ exploration, and Arecibo was the most sensitive instrument of its kind for over two decades.
method: The paper reviews the basics of planetary radar techniques and summarizes key observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo radar observations significantly advanced our understanding of planetary surfaces and subsurface properties, and played a crucial role in characterizing near-Earth objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system left a lasting scientific legacy, and its loss underscores the need for future planetary radar capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo Observatory's contributions to radio astronomy, including pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo 305-m telescope and its upgrades over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and synthesis of key observational results from Arecibo's operations.
result: Arecibo made seminal contributions to pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, VLBI imaging, SETI, and the detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled a wide range of discoveries, cementing its place as a leading radio observatory until its collapse.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science using the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere are highlighted.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar technique and presents results from Arecibo's suite of instruments.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are summarized.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and fundamental physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors synthesize insights from experiments, theory, and computational models of convection-cloud chambers.
result: Convection-cloud chambers reproduce key phenomena like turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentration and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on modeling and detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods in ground-based laser interferometers within multimessenger strategies.
result: The review presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, but does not introduce new results.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova would significantly advance our understanding of the explosion mechanism and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by examining a discrepancy between the observed matter dipole and the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessment of biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their observational signatures.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test beyond-standard-model physics through astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models of self-interacting dark matter and comparison with observational data from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable hypothesis, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers a new opportunity to discover it.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have narrowed the viable parameter space, but several well-motivated scenarios remain testable at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: The HL-LHC will significantly extend the reach for supersymmetry, though discovery is not guaranteed.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No novel research results; a retrospective on scientific discovery.
conclusion: Physics is a point of view that shapes how we understand the world.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a classical machine learning model, with no direct connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in machine learning.
method: The paper describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines are a foundational model for unsupervised learning and have influenced deep learning.
conclusion: The work is a major contribution to machine learning but not to quantum information theory.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but the paper's focus is nuclear astrophysics, not the user's research areas.
method: The paper summarizes theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: It provides a state-of-the-art review of theoretical methods for studying stellar nuclear reactions.
conclusion: The paper concludes that new experimental and theoretical ideas are needed to study these reactions on Earth.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics such as turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
result: The paper highlights key advances and offers insights to enhance modeling of two-phase flow systems.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, bridging the gap between optical and ultrasound imaging.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches enhancing its capabilities.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nonlinear elasticity theory for buckling, creases, and cusps in growing soft matter, with applications in materials science and biology.
motivation: Understanding the formation of creases and cusps during buckling of soft materials is important for morphogenesis and swelling of gels.
method: The review integrates techniques from nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, including bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and elliptic integrals.
result: It provides a modern treatment of the Biot instability and the nonlinear phenomena accompanying surface buckling.
conclusion: The paper offers a comprehensive overview of nonlinear elasticity in soft matter growth, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
